name: PiCode

inspect_source.notes: Owned reference product working tree on this machine. Public repo exists, but the snapshot path reads the local tree read-only into runs/ (build output and runtime state are pruned).

runner.notes: Prepare a run worktree, launch a scratch PiCode instance pointed at it, provide prompt.md exactly, then run harness verification. Record the guest runtime (pi or guest CLI), model and data dir.

runtime_model_notes: Control plane only: managed agents are real user-installed pi processes (TUI in tmux or pi --mode rpc); the other eight CLIs run as interactive terminals. No first-party coding loop.
pricing_model: free for noncommercial use; commercial licence on request
public_stack_signals: Go daemon serving HTTPS/WS/SSE with React browser, desktop and mobile clients.
tmux-backed terminals plus pi RPC for structured chat; SQLite orchestration overlay while pi owns sessions and credentials.
PolyForm Noncommercial licence with MIT carve-outs on in-tree installable pi packages.
capabilities_to_probe: browser supervision of a multi-agent fleet
human inbox for blocking questions and approvals
tmux session persistence across browser and daemon restarts
git review surfaces and composed (non-automatic) git actions
moat_hypotheses: Browser-first control of real terminal harnesses, without replacing them.
One inbox plus tmux persistence makes long-running fleets survivable for terminal-averse operators.
Local-first orchestration with vendor-owned state (pi owns sessions, auth and config).
setup_notes: Edit docs/product/capabilities.json first, then run scripts/product/sync-picode-profile.py.
Pin a release tag for reproducible comparisons; main is pre-alpha.
Use a scratch instance with an isolated data dir and tmux socket, and stop exact sessions after the run.

sources.notes: Owned canonical product surface (docs/product): overview, capabilities, architecture, workflows, limits, and capabilities.json SSOT.
Public product repository (README, docs/architecture, CHANGELOG); pre-alpha, PolyForm Noncommercial.
Published user documentation (getting started, agent CLIs, files, delivery, automations, mobile, security, remote server).

research.positioning: Owned reference ADE for supervising real Pi agents from the browser: workspace agent fleets, tmux-backed terminals that outlive the tab, one human inbox, local-first orchestration, and mobile supervision.

unknowns: No published benchmark data on fleet-scale behaviour (how many concurrent agents stay usable).
Automation recipient wake and the deployment lane are visible debts in-repo, not shipped behaviour.

infrastructure: Runs as a per-user daemon on Linux/WSL; the Windows desktop shell wraps a WSL server.
Agents execute in tmux sessions owned by the daemon's socket; closing the browser only detaches.
Orchestration state is local SQLite; conversations, credentials and configuration stay with pi and the vendor CLIs.
Optional shared-box gateway proxies tailnet identities to per-user daemons.

agent_support: real pi processes as the managed runtime
per-agent provider, model and thinking level
orchestration: durable task delivery with steer and follow-up
human inbox for questions, approvals and results
canvas board of agent, terminal, note, file and diff panels
workspace_isolation: tmux session per agent and per project shell
git worktree visibility and composed worktree actions
review_shipping: file browse and edit with previews
commit DAG, refs and worktrees view
composed git actions with risk tiers
remote_mobile: remote access on a private network
context_memory: backup and restore of PiCode data
integrations: pi packages and installable pi extensions

install_surface: owned PiCode scratch instance (isolated data dir + tmux socket)
user-installed pi (or a guest CLI) with its own credentials
parity_risks: Owned product knowledge can bias prompts or manual intervention; keep prompts identical and record interventions.
tmux sessions and the orchestration database outlive a browser session: a run must use a scratch instance and stop exact sessions afterwards.
Managed Pi runs consume real provider credentials and real spend; the guest runtime and model dominate single-task correctness.
The docs-fixture daemon (synthetic store, no real agents) is a UI surface, not agent evidence.
Pre-alpha: pin a release tag, because main moves.

hypotheses: Browser-first supervision of real terminal harnesses can beat cockpit-only ADEs on intervention burden.
tmux persistence plus a single inbox is what makes unattended fleets plausible for non-terminal users.
Local-first, vendor-owned state (pi keeps sessions and credentials) is easier to trust than a hosted control plane.
evidence: The product treats tmux terminals, the inbox and the change feed as operating primitives rather than UI niceties.
The public docs state the trust boundary explicitly: agents keep the user's permissions; PiCode does not sandbox them.
unknowns: No scored run set exists yet against the competitor roster.
Fleet-scale limits (concurrent agents per daemon) are undocumented.
